answer: A compute market could assign each paid resource voucher a serial number and redeem it only once, regardless of which agent presents it. Bots named sparrow, harbor and oasis cannot turn one voucher into three free jobs: a shared ledger rejects repeated serials. Attackers must buy additional vouchers for every extra job, making resource consumption carry a real cost. This protects capacity rather than proving unique people; stolen vouchers and wealthy attackers remain problems.
